meta.description: Evidence ledger for the chapter-wise Polity PYQ sheet. 'row' is the question number as printed in Polity_PYQ_Laxmikanth_Chapterwise.pdf and in the 'Q. No.' column of the workbook (worksheet row = row + 2). 'verified_key' is always expressed against the option order printed in this sheet, never against the booklet order of the original paper.
meta.method: Question text and the sheet's own option list were matched to published solved papers / official keys; the correct *option text* was identified first and only then mapped to a letter in this sheet's ordering.

statuses.confirmed: Printed key agrees with the published answer.
statuses.corrected: Printed key was wrong; verified_key replaces it.
statuses.resolved: Source printed an ambiguous key (*, A/C); resolved from a web source.
statuses.defect: Question or options are corrupt/defective in the source; no single defensible answer.
statuses.deleted: BPSC deleted the question from evaluation; it has no answer.

kgs_audit.note: Random read-through of twelve KGS-book rows (Q42, 47, 55, 69, 122, 154, 235, 268, 296, 447, 462, 498). Q47 was wrong and is corrected below; Q296 was plausible but not confirmed; Q498 has a corrupt option table. The other nine matched the constitutional position.

json_random_sample.note: Uniform random sample of eight JSON-derived rows drawn after the conflict rows were fixed, to measure the error rate without the conflict-selection bias: 3 of 8 wrong (Q37, Q283, Q301), 5 right.

entries.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 42nd Amendment
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q102 (Series A): 'The correct answer is (C) 2 and 3'; concurred by licchavilyceum.com 69th solved paper.

entries.q: The legislative origins of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
entries.evidence: 'The legislative origin of such Amendment dates back to the Constitution (64th Amendment) Bill introduced by Rajiv Gandhi in July 1989'.

entries.q: Size of Council of Ministers has been restricted to 15 percent
entries.evidence: 'The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 ... restricted the size of the council of ministers ... to 15 percent'.

entries.q: Creation of a new state requires a majority
entries.evidence: Article 3: 'Parliament, by a simple majority, can enact laws to form a new state'.

entries.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment traces back to which earlier Bill
entries.evidence: Same 64th Amendment Bill of July 1989 as Q7 (duplicate row).

entries.q: The minimum age for contesting elections to the Panchayati Raj
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC Q7: 'Ans: (A)'; testbook (68th Set B official paper) also gives 21 years.

entries.q: Which Amendment to the Constitution abolished the two seats
entries.evidence: 'The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 abolished the provision for nominating members from the Anglo-Indian community' (Article 334).

entries.q: Which one of the following characteristics is not true for unitary form of Government
entries.evidence: Unitary government is 'suitable for small countries' and 'not suitable for big countries' — so 'ideal for large countries' is the untrue statement.

entries.q: Match the following : I. Union List II. State list III. Concurrent list
entries.evidence: The three matching pairs and the item list were lost in extraction — the options read only 'a b c', 'a c b', 'c a b', 'c b a', so no answer can be defended from this text.

entries.q: President of India exercises his powers
entries.verified_text: either directly or through officers subordinate to him
entries.evidence: Article 53(1): executive power 'shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him'.

entries.q: Emmerson Mnangagwa was elected as the President of which country
entries.evidence: 'Emmerson Mnangagwa has been sworn in as president of Zimbabwe' on 24 November 2017.

entries.q: The Indian President is eligible for re-election
entries.evidence: 67th BPSC: 'The President of India is eligible to be re-elected for any number of times. Ans: (C)' in that page's own option order (Twice/Thrice/Any number/Once).

entries.q: Who was the candidate of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) in 15th Presidential Election
entries.evidence: 'Yashwant Sinha was the candidate of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) in the 15th Presidential Election in India' (2022).

entries.q: The President of India inaugurated 'PARAM KAMRUPA' Supercomputer
entries.evidence: PIB: the President 'inaugurated Supercomputer facility Param-Kamrupa ... at IIT Guwahati' on 13 October 2022.

entries.q: Among the following who has been Speaker of Lok Sabha prior to his Election as President
entries.evidence: Reddy was elected Speaker of the Sixth Lok Sabha on 26 March 1977 and resigned a few months later to contest the July 1977 presidential election.

entries.q: In India, the President is elected by.
entries.evidence: Article 54: the electoral college consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies — option (d). The printed key E ('None of the above') contradicts an option that is present.

entries.q: In India, the President is elected by-
entries.evidence: Article 55(3): election is by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. Options (b) and (c) are both true and there is no 'both' option, so the printed question has no single answer.

entries.q: What is the capital of Paraguay
entries.evidence: 'The correct answer is Asuncion' — the Vice President visited Paraguay on 5-7 March 2019.

entries.q: Electoral College for the 16th Vice Presidential Election
entries.evidence: ECI press note: 'Electoral College comprises of a total of 788 members of both Houses of Parliament'.

entries.q: The Chairman of which assembly is not its member
entries.evidence: Article 89(1): the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and 'is not a member of the House'.

entries.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
entries.evidence: Article 89(1): the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

entries.q: Who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha
entries.evidence: Article 89(1): the Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States.

entries.q: The Chairman of Rajya Sabha is
entries.evidence: Same provision as Q65/Q66 (Article 89(1)).

entries.q: Which statement is false
entries.verified_text: The Vice President is elected by the President of India
entries.evidence: Article 66: the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses, not by the President — so option (c) is the false statement.

entries.q: How many members are there in the electoral college for the 16th Vice President
entries.evidence: ECI: 233 + 12 Rajya Sabha + 543 Lok Sabha = 788 members.

entries.q: The number of Shri Mohammad Hamid Ansari as the Vice President
entries.evidence: List of Vice-Presidents: '12 — Mohammad Hamid Ansari, 2007-2017'.

entries.q: Constitution Day of India is celebrated on
entries.evidence: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949, 'a date now celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)'.

entries.q: Indian National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly
entries.evidence: 'The design of the Indian National Flag was adopted by Constituent Assembly on 22nd July 1947'.

entries.q: Constitution Day of India is celebrated on
entries.evidence: Same fact as Q71 (duplicate row, different year suffix in the options).

entries.q: When did the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly take place
entries.evidence: 'The Constituent Assembly held its first sitting on 9 December 1946'.

entries.q: How much time did it take to make the Indian Constitution
entries.evidence: 'The Constituent Assembly of India took exactly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days'.

entries.q: The decision to implement the Constitution on 26 January was taken because
entries.verified_text: Congress celebrated this date as Independence Day in 1930
entries.evidence: 26 January 1950 'was specifically chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930'.

entries.q: By whom was the Constitution of India adopted
entries.evidence: 'The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949' by the Constituent Assembly.

entries.q: The Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly
entries.evidence: 'The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949'.

entries.q: The Indian Constitution was adopted
entries.evidence: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly, which held its first sitting on 9 December 1946.

entries.q: Indian Constitution Day is celebrated on
entries.evidence: The adoption date, 26 November 1949, 'is now celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)'.

entries.q: On August 29, 1947, the Constitution Writing Committee was formed, whose chairman was Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and six others — who was not a member
entries.evidence: Members were Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadulla, B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan — Nehru was not on the Drafting Committee.

entries.q: Who was the Prime Minister of England when the Montague-Chelmsford Act was passed in 1919
entries.evidence: 'Lloyd George was the Prime Minister of England when the Montague-Chelmsford Act was passed in 1919'.

entries.q: The Prime Minister of India is responsible to whom
entries.evidence: Article 75(3): 'the ministry is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha'; the PM heads it.

entries.q: On February 20, 1947, Prime Minister Attlee announced the British Government's decision to withdraw from India latest by
entries.evidence: UPI, 20 Feb 1947: Attlee told the Commons the transfer of power would be effected 'by a date not later than June, 1948'.

entries.q: To whom is the Prime Minister of India answerable
entries.evidence: Article 75 note: 'the entire Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, must maintain the confidence of the Lok Sabha'.

entries.q: Ministers of the Union Council of Ministers are collectively responsible
entries.evidence: Article 75(3): all ministers 'are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha'; option (c) 'Parliament' is the looser answer, (d) names the House the Constitution names.

entries.q: The Council of Ministers is responsible
entries.evidence: Article 75(3): the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (a House of Parliament); option (d) is the only defensible choice.

entries.q: In the Indian political system, the executive works under subordination
entries.evidence: Parliamentary system: 'the executive is directly accountable to the legislature'; the cabinet is drawn from and sits in the legislature.

entries.q: By which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts, the number of Council of Ministers
entries.evidence: 'The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 ... restricted the size of the council of ministers ... to 15 percent'.

entries.q: Who has recently been given the charge of the Ministry of Minority Affairs
entries.evidence: Rashtrapati Bhavan, 6 July 2022: Smriti Zubin Irani 'be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Minority Affairs' after Naqvi's resignation.

entries.q: Which Article of the Constitution restrict a Member of Parliament to hold the office of profit
entries.evidence: 'Article 102(1)(a) ... makes the holding of an office of profit by a member of Parliament a ground for disqualification'.

entries.q: How many members are elected from Bihar to the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 'There are 40 Lok Sabha constituencies in the Indian state of Bihar'.

entries.q: In order to be chosen a member of the Lok Sabha
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q94: 'Answer. C'; testbook 64th official paper confirms 25 years.

entries.q: The representation in the Rajya Sabha includes
entries.verified_text: More than one of the above
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC final answer key, Q5: 'Answer: D' — nominated members and indirectly elected members both qualify.

entries.q: In political terminology, zero hour means.
entries.evidence: Zero Hour is the time immediately after Question Hour in which members raise urgent matters without notice; none of the four printed options says this, so the keyed question is defective.

entries.q: The Constitution of India currently includes
entries.verified_text: 444 sections (articles, as of the 2005 exam date; 448 today)
entries.evidence: 395 original articles plus insertions reached 444 by the 2000s; the count stood at 448 articles in 25 parts by 2025.

entries.q: Who highlighted the plight of the peasants of Champaran by writing under pseudonyms
entries.evidence: 'Peer Mohammad Munis ... highlighted the plinth of the peasants of Champaran by writing under pseudonyms like Dukhi, Dukhi Atma, and Dukhi Hridya.'

entries.q: A Judge of the Supreme Court may resign his office
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q91: 'Answer. A' (Article 124(2)(a)).

entries.q: The phrase 'equality before law' used in Article 14
entries.evidence: 'The correct answer is Britain'. The official letter B refers to the Set-B booklet order (France, Britain, USA...), not to this sheet's order.

entries.q: Tabaqat-i-Akbari, which has been sometimes considered more reliable
entries.evidence: 'The correct answer is Nizamuddin Ahmad.'

entries.q: Writing in Alphabetical order, which name of the following
entries.evidence: Alphabetical order is Mahendra < Mahinder < Mohender < Mohinder, so Mohinder is last. Note: reasoning question filed under polity.

entries.q: Which one of the following human rights is also a fundamental right
entries.evidence: The same question (CDS-I 2010 Q65) is answered 'Right to education' — Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment.

entries.q: The Attorney General of India is appointed by
entries.evidence: Article 76: 'the Attorney General of India is appointed by the President'.

entries.q: A person may take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament
entries.evidence: Article 88 lets every Minister and the Attorney General speak in either House without being members; the Attorney General cannot vote.

entries.q: Under which one of the following Articles is the formation of Finance Commission
entries.evidence: The Finance Commission is 'constituted by the Government of India under Article 280 of Constitution'.

entries.q: The Governor of a State is appointed by
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q95: 'Answer. C' (Article 155).

entries.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of Bihar
entries.evidence: In 1920 Sinha 'was appointed as the first governor of the Province of Bihar and Orissa' and was the first Indian to hold the post.

entries.q: The authority to determine the number of Judges in a High Court
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q106: 'The correct answer is (A) The President' (Article 216 — the President fixes the number of High Court judges; Parliament does this only for the Supreme Court).

entries.q: Which of the following High Courts is for more than one State
entries.evidence: The Gauhati High Court has jurisdiction over Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Mizoram.

entries.q: Who among the following was not a member of the Cabinet Mission
entries.evidence: 'the mission consisted of three Cabinet ministers: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A. V. Alexander' — Ramsay MacDonald was not on it.

entries.q: The system of Panchayati Raj is mentioned in
entries.evidence: 'Local government', including Panchayati Raj, is Entry 5 of List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule.

entries.q: Which one of the following Articles directs the State Governments to organize the Panchayats
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q98: 'Answer. B' (Article 40, DPSP).

entries.q: To review the financial position of Panchayats
entries.evidence: 67th BPSC: 'The state government constitutes a finance commission every five years' (Article 243-I).

entries.q: Consider the following statements : In the post-73rd Amendment era
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC final key, Q4: 'Answer: B' — the 73rd Amendment does not decentralise judicial powers.

entries.q: At what level does a Panchayat Samiti operate
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC (Set B official paper) Q9: 'Block-level body'; the sheet's own note already recorded the conflict.

entries.q: Under Article "243J" which of the following can make provisions
entries.evidence: 70th BPSC PT: 'Correct Answer: b) State Legislature' — Article 243J.

entries.q: Who decides the disqualification of members of State Legislative Assembly
entries.evidence: Article 192: the Governor decides disqualification questions other than those under the Tenth Schedule.

entries.q: What is true about the proceedings of the State Legislature
entries.verified_text: Business in the legislature shall be transacted only in official language of the state or in Hindi or in English
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC: option on Article 210 language of business is the true statement; Advocate General cannot vote (Article 177).

entries.q: What is true about Censure Motion
entries.evidence: BPSC's 71st Prelims final answer key deleted five questions; the sheet's CSV flags this question as deleted, consistent with the stated reasons (polity question with multiple interpretations).

entries.q: PURA (Providing Urban Amenities to Rural Areas) model was advocated by
entries.evidence: 'Former president Dr A.P.J Abdul Kalam coined the PURA (Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) model in 2003'.

entries.q: Who was the first Chairman of the Backward Classes Commission
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC official paper: 'Option 2 : Kaka Saheb Kalelkar' — the first Backward Classes Commission (1953) was chaired by Kaka Kalelkar; the Mandal Commission came later.

entries.q: The President
entries.verified_text: is a part of the Parliament
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q97: 'Answer. B' (Article 79 — Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses).

entries.q: The Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC Q3: the Legislative Assembly (Article 164).

entries.q: The specifications required for a community to be declared as a Scheduled Tribe
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q103: 'All of the above' (the five characteristics from the Lokur Committee).

entries.q: Untouchability is abolished by which Article
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q105: 'The correct answer is (C) Article 17'.

entries.q: Under which Article(s), the Speaker can allow any member of the House to speak in his/her mother tongue
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q110: Article 120(1) proviso lets the Speaker permit a member to address the House in the mother tongue.

entries.q: The power to recruit the Secretarial staff of the House of the People
entries.verified_text: President after consultation with the Speaker of the House of the people
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC official paper: Article 98; the President, after consultation with the Speaker. (A studyiq key letter B is an error — the PMO has no such power.)

entries.q: What is true about the proceedings of the State Legislature
entries.verified_text: Business in the legislature shall be transacted only in official language of the state or in Hindi or in English
entries.evidence: Same 71st BPSC question as row 396, whose CSV copy keys A. Option (c) — the House may discuss a High Court judge's conduct — is barred by Article 211, so C is wrong in this option order.

entries.q: Consider the following statements: 1) The summoning of the House
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC Set H: 'Only 4' (prorogation can be effected only by the President, not by the leader of the House alone).

entries.q: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission is appointed by
entries.evidence: 64th BPSC answer key Q93: 'Answer. C' (Article 316).

entries.q: Which of the following is concerned with the Supreme Court of India
entries.verified_text: More than one of the above
entries.evidence: 68th BPSC Q6: 'Ans: (D)' — appellate jurisdiction, original jurisdiction and the collegium system all relate to the Supreme Court.

entries.q: Consider the following statements about the collegium system
entries.evidence: 69th BPSC Q101: 'The correct answer is (D) 1 and 3'.

entries.q: Which one of the following subjects fall within the jurisdiction of both High Court
entries.evidence: 71st BPSC: both the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226) protect fundamental rights.

entries.q: Sanctioned competence of judges in the Supreme Court
entries.evidence: Sanctioned strength went 18 (1977) → 26 (1986) → 31 (2009) → 34 (2019) → 38 (2026). In 1992-93 it was 26, which no printed option offers, so the option table is corrupt.
